The factual matrix of the case is that the Plaintiffs/ Appellants herein, in the year 1988, filed a Suit for permanent prohibitory injunction before the Trial Court against the Defendants/
Respondents with respect to a piece of land measuring 08 Marlas comprised of Survey No. 85 situate at Qasba Bala, Nowshera, stating therein that the Defendants/ Respondents, without any right, title, claim or interest over the aforesaid 08 Marlas of land, tried to encroach upon the same Tara Wanti vs State Of J&K Through Chief Secretary on 8 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7150575/

sentences.text: 03. The Defendants/ Respondents appeared before the Trial Court and filed their Written Statement in opposition to the said Suit.

It was stated that the Suit land was acquired by the Government from the husband of Plaintiff No.1/ Appellant No.1 herein in the year 1962-63 and that the Defendants/
Respondents herein are in possession of the Suit land since then.
They further averred that they raised construction on the Suit land in the shape of Labour Sarai of the Labour Department, road and the construction of NAC, Nowshera.

It was also averred that the Plaintiffs/ Appellants herein have never been in possession of the Suit land and that the Plaintiffs/ Appellants herein had sold the land in Survey No. 85 to different persons and kept the land for lanes and drains, as such, there remained no land with the owner in Survey No. 85.

It had been further pleaded by the Defendants/
Respondents herein that there was a barbed wire fence put by the Defendants/ Respondents herein which was being replaced by a solid wall.
It was urged that the Suit land belonged to and is in possession of the Defendants/ Respondents, as such, the Suit filed by the Plaintiffs/ Appellants deserved to be dismissed.

04. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, the learned Trial Court framed the following issues for the trial of the case:
1.

Whether Suit land measuring 08 Marlas comprising Khasra No. 85 of Qasba Bala,
Nowshera is in ownership and possession of the Plaintiffs?

OPP;
2.
Whether the Defendants want to take possession of the Suit land illegally by forcibly constructing retention wall (Dangah) around it?

OPP; and CFA No. 24/2005 c/w 3. Relief?

Thereafter, the parties led their evidence, documentary as well as oral, before the learned Trial Court.

The Plaintiffs/ Appellants herein recorded the statement of their authorized Attorney,
namely, Labu Ram, being well conversant with the facts of the case.
In addition to his statement, the statements of six other persons were also recorded by the Plaintiffs/ Appellants for establishing the possession on the Suit land.
The Defendants/ Respondents also recorded the statements of as many as six witnesses.

06. The learned Trial Court, after hearing the parties and appreciating the evidence brought on record, decided all the issues in favour of the Defendants/ Respondents and against the Plaintiffs/
Appellants and dismissed the Suit vide Judgment and Decree dated 30th of May, 2002.

i. That the Suit land was shown in actual physical possession of the plaintiffs as per the revenue record, copies whereof were duly proved by the Patwari's concerned.
Any oral evidence to the contrary was/ is not admissible in Evidence Act;
ii. That the revenue entries duly recorded in ordinary course by the competent Revenue Officers carry a legal presumption of their correctness.

It is admitted case of the respondent/ State that only 10 Marlas of the land has been acquired and the suit land is beyond 10 Marlas so acquired.

Thus, the claim of the respondents that the suit land was part of the acquired land is without any basis, record and evidence, same deserves to be set aside;
iv.
That admittedly land (subject matter of the suit) was/ is shown to be in actual possession of the owners/ appellants.
The findings of the Courts below that the revenue entries have no evidentiary value are without any legal sanction and is liable to be set aside; and CFA No. 24/2005 c/w vi.

Appellant shall make his submissions regarding the true import of the judgment.

10. Aggrieved of the aforesaid Judgment passed by the learned First Appellate Court, the Appellants have filed the present Civil Second Appeal before this Court on the following substantial questions of law:
i. Whether the Trial Courts were justified in misinterpreting documentary evidence or not considering material evidence and ignoring admissions and concessions made by defendants and their witnesses during the trial?

ii. Whether the Courts below were justified in ignoring the entries contained in the revenue record, namely, the record of rights (Jamabandi) and annual records (Khasra Girdawaries), showing the title and possession of the plaintiff without any challenge to the same in accordance with law?
iii. Whether the Courts below were justified in not considering the spot inspection reports prepared by the revenue officers and duly annexed before the Trial Court.
The observations of Trial Courts regarding the admissibility of these documents are contrary to the provisions of Evidence Act?
iv. Whether the Courts below were not required to follow the settled proposition of law that "POSSESSION FOLLOWS TITLE", where the land is not in physical possession of any person other than owners?
v. Whether the findings of the Trial Court on Hearsay Evidence can be said to be legal and binding and whether the same can be formed basis for dismissal of the suit?
vi. Whether the Trial Courts were justified in passing the judgment which is perverse and contrary to the evidence on record?

who claimed to be the Attorney Holder of the Appellants, PW-1 Sunit Singh Patwari, PW-2 Haveli Ram, PW-3 Jagdish Lal, PW-5 Katab Hussain Patwari, PW-7 Talib Hussain Patwari, Defendant No.4-Mulkh Raj Sharma, Labour Commissioner, DW-1 Bachan Singh, Assistant Commissioner,

He has further argued that the Trial Court as well as the First Appellate Court have not appreciated that the title and possession of the CFA No. 24/2005 c/w Plaintiffs/ Appellants, which was recorded in the Record of Rights (Jamabandi) and Annual Records (Khasra Girdawaries), carry a strong legal and statutory presumption under Section 31 of the Land Revenue Act and that if any person was aggrieved of an entry in the revenue record, and for the possession of the right claimed if the said aggrieved person is not in possession thereof within one year from the date of publication of the record, such an aggrieved person may have to institute a Suit before the Collector/ Deputy Commissioner for the correction of the said record, however, no such Suit has ever been filed by the Respondents before any Revenue Officer in terms of Section 32 of the Land Revenue Act.

He has argued that in the last inspection report conducted and prepared by the Tehsildar, Agrarian Reforms on 6 th of February, 1990, it is evidently clear that the Food and Supplies Department was in possession of 15 Marlas of land and 08 Marlas of land was vacant which was adjoining the road, though such a spot inspection report was a document having legal bearings and its exclusion is contrary to the provisions of the Evidence Act.

The learned Senior Counsel further argued that the Courts below were required to follow the settled proposition of law that "possession follows title", where the land is not in physical possession of any person other than owners and that even if there was no evidence of possession of Plaintiffs/

He has further argued that the Courts below were not justified in passing the impugned Judgments, which are perverse and CFA No.

Therefore, the Defendants/ Respondents had failed to non-suit the Plaintiffs/ Appellants and, as such, the Suit was required to be decreed in absence of any right established by the Defendants/ Respondents qua the Suit land.

21. Mr Ravinder Gupta, the learned Additional Advocate General, appearing for the official Respondents, on the other hand, argued that the Suit land forming the subject matter of this appeal was admitted to be adjacent to a Labour Sarai constructed by the Labour Department at Nowshera,
raised on an acquired piece of land.

The Appellants/ Plaintiffs, in their own pleadings, had admitted before the Courts below that the Labour Sarai had been constructed by the official Respondents on a land acquired from one Ram Parkash, predecessor-in-interest of the Appellants as well as Respondent No.5.

Therefore, the Appellants/ Plaintiffs are CFA No. 24/2005 c/w estopped in law from raising such a plea with regard to their possession over the land having been acquired as per their own admission for the construction of Labour Sarai, as such, the Trial Court had rightly dismissed the Suit and the First Appellate Court had also rightly decided the Appeal rejecting the same and upholding the impugned Judgment and Decree passed by the learned Trial Court.

sentences.text: The Appellants/ Plaintiffs had filed a Civil Original Suit before the Trial Court through their Attorney, seeking issuance of a perpetual injunction against the Respondents/ Defendants restraining them from raising the boundary wall or to interfere in any manner in the Suit land bearing Survey No. 85 measuring 08 Marlas situated at Qasba Bala, Nowshera.

On notice having been issued by the Trial Court, the official Respondents appeared, whileas, the private Respondent No.5, Vijay Kumar, chose not to contest the Suit, whereafter, on the basis of pleadings available and evidence on record, the Trial Court concluded that the following facts have emerged.

29. Taking the whole stock of evidence into consideration, the Trial Court came to the conclusion that the Plaintiffs have failed to prove their possession, much less of continuous possession, over the Suit land, rather it was revealed that the Plaintiffs have failed to prove their possession over the Suit land and have ventured to occupy the Suit land, which remained uncared and out of the reach of the Labour Department for most of the time since the construction of the Labour Sarai.
A portion of the Sarai was still in use and occupation of the Revenue Department as the office of Tehsildar, Agrarian.
Finally, in view of these facts, the issue No.1 was declared to have not been proved in favour of the Plaintiffs.

The second issue, being dependent on the outcome of the first issue, therefore, there was no question of the Defendants trying to occupy the Suit land forcibly, as alleged and, as such, this issue was also decided in favour of the Defendants and against the Plaintiffs.
Accordingly, on the basis of the findings returned on both the issues, the Suit of the Appellants/ Plaintiffs came to be dismissed along with costs.

Aggrieved of the Judgement and Decree passed by the learned Trial Court, the Appellants/
Plaintiffs filed Civil Second Appeal before the First Appellate Court.

Initially, the Suit was filed by the Appellants/ Plaintiffs along with the Respondent No.5, Vijay Kumar as Plaintiff No.4, however,
the Plaintiff No.4, Vijay Kumar, was transposed as proforma Defendant No.4 in the Plaintiffs' case,
on an application filed by him.

It is pertinent to mention here that the Plaintiff No.4 had sought withdrawal CFA No. 24/2005 c/w from the Suit to which other Plaintiffs objected to and, as such, he was transposed as proforma Defendant vide Order dated 1st of February, 1993.
31.

The Plaintiffs, in their Plaint, had pleaded that out of the Survey Number 85, the Plaintiff-Tara Wanti's husband had sold 10 Marlas of land to the Public Works Department, on which they had constructed the Labour Sarai and some other portion was sold to the Government and land measuring 01 Kanal and 01 Marlas was left with them.

The Defendant No.4, Assistant Labour Commissioner, Rajouri, in his Written Statement, had asserted that the Suit land was under continuous possession of the Labour Department and was fenced with barbed wire and that mulberry trees had been planted in the Suit land.

32. The Defendant Nos. 1 to 3, in their Written Statement, refuted the averments made by the Plaintiffs and claimed that the Suit land was owned by the Government and was used as compound since 1962-63, when it had been acquired and that the Plaintiffs had no right over the land in dispute.

33. Before the First Appellate Court, the Respondents raised a plea that none of the Plaintiffs had appeared in the Witness Box in support of their case and, instead, their Power of Attorney, PW-Labu Ram, had appeared on their behalf and that no reliance can be placed on his testimony in view of the Judgment of the Apex Court in case titled 'Janki v. Indusind Bank Limited', reported as 'AIR 2005 SC 439'; wherein it had been held in respect of the deposition of a Power of Attorney that the Power of Attorney holder does not have personal knowledge of the matter of the Appellants and, therefore,
he can neither depose on his personal knowledge nor can he be cross-examined on those facts which are of the personal knowledge of the principal.

sentences.text: In the said Judgment, the Apex Court, while discussing Rules 1 and 3 of Order III of the Code of Civil Procedure, had explained the aforesaid principle.

The First Appellate Court, while discussing that whether the Plaintiffs and their predecessor-in-interest had sold the Suit land, can only be explained by the Plaintiffs themselves and not by their Power of Attorney holder, who does not have personal CFA No. 24/2005 c/w knowledge of those matters, so he can neither depose on his personal knowledge nor he can be cross-examined on these facts which are to the personal knowledge of the principal.

It was observed that the non- appearance of the Plaintiffs in the Witness Box counts against the interests of the Plaintiffs and it has to be rightly held that they have failed to prove their case that they are in possession of the Suit land and that the Defendants interfered with their possession over the Suit land.

34. Apart from that, the First Appellate Court further observed that the other evidence adduced by the Plaintiffs did not prove the case set up by them, inasmuch as, PW-Labu Ram deposed that the Plaintiffs did not allow the Defendants to use the Suit land, whereas, PW-Haweli Ram deposed that the Defendants were using the Suit land at the time the office of Food and Supplies Department was Tara Wanti vs State Of J&K Through Chief Secretary on 8 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7150575/

sentences.text: It may be mentioned that the first appellate court under Section 96 CPC is the last court of facts.
